edges.notes: fetch(`/api/task?workspaceId=${workspace.id}`, { method: "POST" }), root-relative on the same Next app (apps/next-web is the only Next app; middleware.ts's matcher skips /api/ paths, so no host rewrite); query dropped

fetch(`/api/workspaces/${slug}/exists`), no options so GET; [idOrSlug] => :idOrSlug (only a slug of literally "repo" would hit the literal workspaces/repo/exists folder instead, which exports POST only)
fetch(`/api/workspaces/repo/exists`, { method: "POST" }); the literal repo/ folder wins over [idOrSlug] in Next's dispatch
fetch("/api/workspaces", { method: "POST" }) in the form's onSubmit; the mutate("/api/workspaces") after it only revalidates an SWR key, not labeled
fetch(`/api/workspaces/${id}/invites`, { method: "POST" }); invites/route.ts exports const POST
fetch(`/api/escrow`, { method: "POST" }) after the wallet transaction; the Solana connection calls above it are web3 SDK requests, not labeled
fetch(`/api/payment`, { method: "POST" })
fetch(`/api/task/${taskId}?workspaceId=${workspace.id}`, { method: "PUT" }); [taskId]/route.ts exports PUT only; query dropped
fetch(`/api/transfer?workspaceId=${workspace.id}`, { method: "POST" }); the mutate(...) calls after it only revalidate SWR keys, not labeled
fetch(`/api/wallet?publicKey=${publicKey.toString()}`), no options so GET; query dropped
fetch(`/api/wallet`, { method: "POST" }) when the GET answered 404

Edge middleware: fetch(process.env.NEXT_ADMIN_APP_DOMAIN + `/api/database/admin?userId=…`), no in-code fallback; .env.example sets NEXT_ADMIN_APP_DOMAIN=tesior-admin.xyz, a bare host. The code needs it bare: middleware.ts reaches AdminMiddleware only when ADMIN_HOSTNAMES (lib/utils/constants, holding this value) has the Host header's domain (lib/middleware/utils/parse.ts). So the URL is 'tesior-admin.xyz/api/database/admin?…' with no scheme, which fetch rejects, and the request reaches no route, labeled as written like devcamper's unmatched paths. The route it means is GET /api/database/admin (app/api/database/admin/route.ts line 4)
useSWR(`/api/balance`, fetcher, …): SWR calls the repo's lib/utils.ts fetcher (fetch(input)) with the key, so the path is supplied here; utils.ts:44 itself is not labeled
useSWR(`/api/escrow`, fetcher) with the repo's fetcher
useSWR(`/api/leaderboard`, fetcher) with the repo's fetcher
useSWR(`/api/payment`, fetcher) with the repo's fetcher
useSWR(`/api/task?workspaceId=${workspaceId}`, fetcher) with the repo's fetcher; query dropped
useSWR(`/api/transfer?transfer=${sentOrReceived}&workspaceId=${workspaceId}`, fetcher) with the repo's fetcher; query dropped
useSwr("/api/user", fetcher) (swr's default export imported as useSwr) with the repo's fetcher; user/route.ts exports const GET
useSWRImmutable(fetchApiUrl, fetcher) with fetchApiUrl = `https://api.github.com/users/${username}/repos?…` (line 5): the repo's fetcher sends the key to GitHub's API, an external host
useSWR(id && `/api/workspaces/${id}/users`, fetcher): a conditional key (no request while id is empty) is still labeled with its url
useSWR(slug && `/api/workspaces/${slug}`, fetcher, …): conditional key, labeled with its url
useSWR("/api/workspaces", fetcher, …) with the repo's fetcher
convertDollarToSolana: fetch(`${COINGECKO_API_URL}?ids=solana&vs_currencies=usd`), COINGECKO_API_URL = "https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price" (line 18), an external host
